item.text: Both spoons are probably at the same room temperature, but metal feels colder because it pulls heat from your hand much faster than wood does. Your skin senses the rate at which it loses heat, not just an object’s actual temperature. Metal conducts heat efficiently, so the surface touching your hand quickly warms by taking energy from you. Wood is a poor conductor, so it removes heat slowly and feels comparatively warmer, even though its temperature is the same.
